newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY READY FOR EMU, BACKS QUICKER PROGRESS - CIAMPI.
newsitem.headline: ITALY READY FOR EMU, BACKS QUICKER PROGRESS - CIAMPI.

text.p: Italy is ready to join Europe's single currency and would support an acceleration of the process towards European monetary and economic union (EMU), Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Thursday.
In an interview with Turin-based La Stampa newspaper, Ciampi said the time had arrived to start discussions on an acceleration of the process towards EMU, which is scheduled to start in January 1999.
"Italy would not raise objections to this (an acceleration of the process), but would understand and share the reasons," Ciampi said.
Ciampi stresed that he was not preoccupied by the recent strength of the dollar, which he said reflected a dynamic economy in the U.S. and not the emergence of economic problems in Europe.

He added that he saw Italian inflation remaining under two percent for the rest of this year, and sees an agreement being reached on welfare spending in September, in time for the 1998 financial budget.

Italy's consumer price index (CPI) inflation stood at 1.6 percent in July on an annual basis after 1.4 percent in June, but the small rise was largely due to statistical reasons and the month-on-month CPI rate was flat for June and July.
